ideas.description: Lengthen the 28 px stage again and price the next half-epoch of the 32 px tail. The tip is E052 (commit 447a7db): bs 1536; 20 px bilinear antialiased whole images for epochs 0-1.5 and 28 px for 1.5-3.5, both without translate; 32 px with translate-2 for 3.5-6.75; jitter in every stage; SGD-group lr x1.5; head lr x2 with wd halved; Muon lr 0.16, mom 0.8, NS3; lookahead 0.97^5; whitening bias trained in epoch 1 only. If I072 (bs 2048 in the low-res stages) is kept, use its commit and keep its batch sizes per stage. Make one change: move the 28 -> 32 px switch from 3.5 to 4.0 epochs (sample 200000), so 28 px runs for 2.5 epochs and 32 px for the last 2.75. The low-res augment variant (no translate) covers the longer 28 px stage. Total epochs, bs, the sample stream and every step-indexed schedule stay unchanged. Where the switch falls inside a step, split that step into the two partial shapes, as the existing switches do. In build(), warm up every new partial-batch shape at the 4.0-epoch switch for the 28 px and 32 px graphs, with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). Keep build under ~450 s. Run debug_nan.py on new shapes and compare trial-0 with later-trial train times.
ideas.expected: Time -0.8% to -2.5%, point -1.5% (~4.85 s vs 4.928 s). Accuracy -0.40 to +0.15 pp, point -0.13 pp (~0.7533, borderline; E051's half-epoch cost -0.10 pp, and the price should rise as the 28 px stage reaches further into peak lr and decay). Feasible and >=1.2% faster: keep, new best. Infeasible by <=0.1 pp: keep the code path and pair it with the next accuracy gain (I082/I083/H6.1.1). A drop >=0.3 pp means the 32 px tail is at its floor near 3.25 epochs; close stage-length tuning and refute H6.3.1's extension.

ideas.description: Gate in drafts/, untimed. The submission changes only if a no-op is found. Check whether earlier hyperparameter edits actually reached the compiled timed path. (1) On the tip, log each lookahead sync's applied alpha and each step's Muon and head lr as read from the 0-d tensors inside the compiled graphs, and check them against the intended schedule. (2) For seed 0, train the E027 and E028 commits (lookahead 0.95^5 vs 0.97^5), E045 and E046 (Muon lr 0.16 vs 0.20), and E047 and E049 (head x2 vs x3). Compare hashes and norms of the final parameters. Pairs that are bit-identical, or applied values that ignore the edit, mean that edit was a compile-time constant or a dead code path. If any axis was a no-op, fix the plumbing (pass the value as a 0-d GPU tensor read inside the graph, warmed up in build()) and rerun the dead axis's original setting on the tip as one experiment: for example lookahead 0.97^5 actually applied. If every pair differs, record H1.6.6 refuted and change nothing.
ideas.expected: Most likely no change to the metrics: all pairs differ, which refutes H1.6.6 and confirms that the flat lookahead/Muon-lr/head axes are really flat. If a no-op is found (~25% chance, mostly E028's lookahead decay), the follow-up experiment moves accuracy by -0.3 to +0.3 pp at unchanged time and reopens H1.6.1. Either way it removes a confound behind 3-4 closed axes for ~no run budget.

ideas.description: FreezeOut-style late freeze of block 1. On the tip (E052, or I072's successor if kept), make one change. For the last 20% of training samples, from 5.4 epochs on, use a third 32 px train-step graph variant in which block 1's output is detached. Its conv filters and BN affine params get no gradient, but block 1 still runs in train mode, so BN running stats keep updating. Pair it with a second compiled Muon-step variant that excludes the 128x1152 block-1 shape group. The backward then skips block 1's wgrad and dgrad and block 2's first-conv dgrad. Pick the variant in Python by sample count, with no data-dependent branch in the graph. Lookahead still blends block 1 as now: the slow weights keep converging to the frozen fast weights. The SGD group skips block-1 BN biases (zero grad) through the same variant flag. In build(), warm up the new train variant and the new Muon variant, including every partial-batch shape at the 5.4-epoch switch, with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). Run debug_nan.py on the new graph and compare trial-0 with later-trial train times.
ideas.expected: Time -1.8% to -4%, point -2.7% (~4.80 s). Block 1 is ~20% of forward FLOPs, and the skipped backward work is ~20% of a 32 px step on ~20% of steps, plus the block-1 Muon group. Accuracy -0.6 to +0.1 pp, point -0.2 pp (~0.7526, likely infeasible alone): E037 showed block-1 capacity matters under Muon, and E025 showed tail diversity feeds the lookahead average. Feasible and >=1.5% faster: keep. Drop <=0.15 pp: keep the code and pair it with the next accuracy gain, or retry with the last 10%. Drop >=0.35 pp: refute H2.4.7; late block-1 updates matter.

ideas.description: Give the 100-way head an orthogonalized update. On the tip (E052, or I072's successor if kept), make one change: move the [100, 576] head weight out of the SGD group into Muon. Add it as its own shape group in the batched compiled Muon step: Nesterov momentum 0.8, NS3 with the same coefficients, sqrt(max(1,out/in)) = 1. Do NOT apply the weight-norm projection to the head, because row norms set the logit scale. Keep the head's current decoupled per-step decay (the same lr*wd product as now). Set its Muon lr so that the first-step update RMS matches the current SGD head's (x2) first-step update RMS, measured in drafts/ on real batch 0 of seed 0, and log that number. Use the same schedule multiplier as the Muon group. The head bias, if present, stays in SGD. In build(), warm up the new Muon graph on synthetic tensors and run debug_nan.py under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.5 to +0.5 pp, point +0.05 pp (structural explore; head lr x0.5 cost 0.41 pp, so the head is sensitive, but its lr axis is flat above x2). Time +0.1% to +0.8% (one small 100x576 NS group). A gain >=0.25 pp supports H1.10.1 and banks margin for the 28 px extension or I057. Within +-0.15 pp: the head's update geometry is not limiting; close H1.10. A drop >=0.3 pp means the SGD head's gradient-weighted directions are useful; refute.

ideas.description: Test whether the early whitening-bias freeze limits the cheap curriculum. On the tip (E052, or I072's successor if kept), make one change: keep training the whitening-conv bias until the end of the 28 px stage (3.5 epochs, sample 175000) instead of until the end of epoch 1. This needs a 28 px train-step variant WITH whitening-bias grad, compiled and warmed up in build() (full batch and every partial shape at the 1.5- and 3.5-epoch switches), with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). The 32 px stage keeps the frozen-bias graph. Lr for the whitening bias follows its existing schedule. Run debug_nan.py on the new graph and compare trial-0 with later-trial train times.
ideas.expected: Time +0.4% to +1.5%, point +0.9% (~4.97 s; block-1 first-conv dgrad at 19-27 px for 2.5 more epochs). Accuracy -0.2 to +0.35 pp, point +0.08 pp. A gain >=0.2 pp supports H6.1.1: the bias fitted only at 20 px is a real handicap. Keep it, since it is worth more than its ~1% time at ~0.05 pp/1%, and pair the margin with the 28 px extension. A change within +-0.1 pp refutes the confound at 20 px; then 18 px (H6.1.2) is limited only by the final-map threshold.

drop.reason: Stale: it was written against the E040 tip (bs 1024, 24 px stage), and the base has since changed through bs 1536, the 20/28 px curriculum, head x2 and the low-res augment. Its required control, H1.2.4 (Muon lr 0.11), has never run, so a positive result could not be told apart from a lower effective lr. The point estimate (-0.05 pp) is also the lowest of the explore candidates. Re-propose H1.9.1 on the current tip only after the H1.2.4 control, or in an RMS-matched form.

The tip is E052 (4.928 s, 0.7546), which leaves only 0.16 pp of margin. I072 (bs 2048 in the low-res stages) is running.

**New ideas (5):**
- **H6.3.1, priority 3:** the main time lever left on the curriculum. Run 28 px through epoch 4.0, leaving 2.75 epochs at 32 px. Expected about -1.5% time at about -0.13 pp, which is borderline feasible.
- **H1.6.6, priority 3:** a cheap check in `drafts/`. It verifies whether the lookahead-decay, Muon-lr and head-lr edits actually reached the compiled path, by logging the values applied and comparing final-weight hashes across commit pairs. This guards against several "flat" axes being compile no-ops.
- **H2.4.7, priority 2:** FreezeOut on block 1 for the last 20% of samples. Expected about -2.7% time at about -0.2 pp. The prior is low, but it is one of the few structural time cuts left.
- **H1.10.1, priority 2:** move the 100-way head onto Muon, with no weight-norm projection and lr set to match the current update RMS. This is the structural explore idea on the update side.
- **H6.1.1, priority 2:** train the whitening bias through the end of the 28 px stage. It tests whether freezing the bias at low resolution limits how cheap the curriculum can get, for about +0.9% time.

**Changes to the existing queue:**
- **Dropped I054 (H1.9.1):** it was written against the old E040 base, and its Muon-lr control (H1.2.4) has never run.
- **Kept:** I057 (bs 2048 throughout; once I072 is read, it only prices the 32 px stage), I064 (BN-bias lr x128), and I068 (an RNG-shift run that measures paired noise).

That brings the queue to 8. The time-cutting ideas are tight against the 0.753 gate. Any idea that lands within about 0.1 pp of the gate should keep its code path and be paired with whichever accuracy idea succeeds.
